# Answer to `generator-shortcuts`

The strongest plausible shortcut is **yellow-density ordering**. The intended rule maps special reference rows to special template rows in top-to-bottom order. The rival instead sorts special reference rows by increasing count of yellow (`4`) cells, breaking ties by row index, and then assigns the template variants in that order.

This is not an arbitrary wrong rule: it fits all **10/10 canonical labeled records** (five unique canonical inputs), just as the two previously declared shortcuts do. Before repair it also fit all three demonstrations of the production lesson `seed=0`, `difficulty=medium`, accepted indices `[7,8,9,10]`, while changing the query.

## How the output was checked

The input was produced through the public generator path and passed both `self_check` and `strict_canonical_like`. The selected Racket rule was executed through the protected catalog runtime; its declared and executed hashes both equal `70d9964daef1`. An independently written parser/oracle in `workspace/reference_probe.py` produced the rival prediction without calling the production parser or mirror. The retained witness verifies source binding to generator SHA `2e9e935392918e4601d5a435bd25dd54644694bb936161335e11ad39191990ca`, rule binding, lawfulness, declaration of the rival, disagreement, and witness firing; every check is `true`.

## Does the proposed generator emit such cases?

Yes. It now emits them intentionally in every noncanonical schedule role rather than accidentally hiding them. On the exact previous lesson recipe, accepted indices `[7,8,9,10]` are unchanged: demonstrations 7 and 8 refute the rival, canonical sample 9 may agree, and query 10 also differs. The lesson hook therefore accepts for the right reason—because the demonstrations distinguish the shortcut (`checks/repair/d5178d26d905-density-order/report.json`).

Across the larger final-source census, 300/300 three-demonstration/one-query lessons materialized and all 1,200 held-out-pair rotations had zero ambiguity against the three declared rivals. Each rival, including yellow-density ordering, was refuted in 100/100 lessons in each of easy, medium, and hard bands (`checks/lesson-census.summary.json`). A separate cyclic probe passed 960/960 rotations over 552 unique inputs. These finite results establish supported-schedule coverage, not universal identifiability.
